On the right, layout_forceatlas2(seed=1) pulls each triangle together and pushes the triangles apart, so they sit as three separate clusters linked in a ring." width="100%"} ForceAtlas2 (Jacomy, Venturini, Heymann & Bastian, 2014) gives every node a mass of its degree plus one. Every pair of nodes repels with force `scaling_ratio * m_i * m_j / d`, so hubs push others away hard; every edge attracts its ends with force `w * d`; and gravity pulls every node toward the centroid with force `gravity * m`, so disconnected pieces don't fly off. Steps adapt as the run goes: nodes whose force keeps swinging back and forth move less, nodes pulled steadily one way move more, and a global speed rises or falls with how much the whole layout swings. The result is centered and scaled so the largest coordinate is `scale=`. The options are the ones in Gephi: - `linlog=True` uses the weaker attraction `w * log(1 + d)`, which separates clusters more sharply (Noack's LinLog energy); - `dissuade_hubs=True` divides each node's attraction by its mass, pushing hubs toward the edge of their cluster and authorities toward the center; - `strong_gravity=True` makes gravity grow with distance, `gravity * m * d`, for a more compact picture; - `node_size=` turns on overlap prevention: distances are measured between node borders, overlapping nodes repel strongly and stop attracting. Each iteration costs `O(n^2)` (run in parallel on larger graphs; Gephi uses a Barnes-Hut approximation instead). Edge direction is ignored and parallel edges add their weights. NetworkX's `forceatlas2_layout()` takes the same parameters (its `distributed_action=` is `dissuade_hubs=` here), but it measures swing from positions rather than successive forces, and it returns unscaled coordinates; the update here follows the paper and Gephi. Positions are stored as `[x, y]` lists in the `attr_name=` node attribute; see `layout_circular()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of iterations.
